paper_records.paper_title: A new mechanical model of short wire ropes: Theory and experimental validation
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2025-A new mechanical model of short wire ropes Theory and experimental.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: 2025-A new mechanical model of short wire ropes Theory and experimental.pdf
paper_records.why_added: State-of-the-art 2025 analytical and experimental formulation of stick-slip flexural mechanics in short wire ropes.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Directly threatens T1, T2, and H0b by formulating exact stick-slip bending bounds under contact friction.
paper_records.method: Analytical continuum beam modeling and experimental static/dynamic bending tests
paper_records.material_or_system: Short multiwire steel wire ropes (19-wire and 49-wire configurations)
paper_records.loading_mode: Three-point bending and cantilever cyclic bending flexure
paper_records.independent_variables: Rope length (short vs long), wire lay geometry, contact normal force distribution
paper_records.dependent_variables: Bending moment-curvature response, stick-slip transition curvature, upper/lower flexural stiffness bounds (EI_stick, EI_slip)
paper_records.model_used: Shear-deformable beam theory with inter-wire tangential slip and normal contact tractions
paper_records.constitutive_model: Linear elastic wire material with inter-wire stick-slip contact equilibrium
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Coulomb friction law with normal contact pressure resulting from internal geometry and clamping
paper_records.experiment_used: Custom bending test rig with digital image correlation and load cells
paper_records.experimental_setup: Wire ropes clamped at ends and loaded laterally to measure moment-curvature and slip thresholds
paper_records.key_results: Derived closed-form equations for stick stiffness bound (EI_stick) and slip stiffness bound (EI_slip); proved that the transition from full stick to full slip depends on normal contact force and friction coefficient; experimental data validated the predictive bounds without parameter fitting.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that beam stick-slip mechanics rigorously predicts the variable flexural stiffness of multiwire bundles under frictional contact.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not incorporate superelastic NiTi phase transformation; steel ropes only.
directly_verified_statements: The flexural rigidity of a multiwire rope transitions smoothly from EI_stick (full composite action) to EI_slip (isolated wire sum) as inter-wire friction is overcome (Section 2, pp. 3-6).
The model predicts both stiffness bounds using only wire geometry and elastic properties without fitting parameters (Section 4, pp. 11-14).
inferred_statements: The mechanics of positive-pressure wire jamming is mathematically isomorphic to the stick-slip transition in short wire ropes, where pressure modulates the normal force.
paper_records.limitations: Linear elastic steel wires; did not evaluate active fluid membrane confinement.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Confirms that variable bending stiffness via contact friction is a solved continuum mechanics problem (H0b competitor).
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Eq. (12)-(15) (stiffness bounds), Fig. 6 (bending moment vs curvature comparison)

paper_records.paper_title: Finite Element Method for Mechanical Behavior of Shape Memory Alloy Superelastic Cables (形状记忆合金超弹性缆索力学行为的有限单元法)
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2025-Finite Element Method for Mechanical Behavior of Shape Memory Alloy .pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: 2025-Finite Element Method for Mechanical Behavior of Shape Memory Alloy .pdf
paper_records.why_added: Branch B11 citation anchor: specialized finite element method for superelastic SMA cables.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Threatens T1 and T3 by demonstrating tailored finite element formulation for contacting NiTi cable structures.
paper_records.method: Nonlinear finite element formulation using corotational beam elements with contact
paper_records.loading_mode: Monotonic and cyclic tension and pure bending
paper_records.independent_variables: Cable lay geometry, friction coefficient, strain amplitude
paper_records.dependent_variables: Hysteresis curves, axial force, bending moment, contact stress distribution along helix
paper_records.model_used: Corotational beam element incorporating Auricchio 1D superelastic constitutive model
paper_records.constitutive_model: 1D Auricchio superelastic constitutive model with tension-compression asymmetry
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Point-to-line and line-to-line contact element with Coulomb friction
paper_records.experiment_used: Comparison against experimental data from Reedlunn 2013
paper_records.experimental_setup: Numerical validation study benchmarking against published experimental cable data
paper_records.key_results: Developed a dedicated beam finite element algorithm capable of simulating large deformation, inter-wire contact, and superelastic phase transformation in NiTi cables with high numerical efficiency and stability.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that existing beam contact finite elements combined with standard 1D Auricchio models (H0b) accurately simulate NiTi multiwire cable deformation.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not apply active external pneumatic/hydraulic confinement pressure.
directly_verified_statements: The corotational beam FE model with 1D Auricchio constitutive relations reproduces the tensile and bending hysteresis of SMA cables (Section 3, pp. 68-71).
Inter-wire contact forces concentrate along helical line contacts and dictate local frictional slip (Section 4, pp. 71-73).
inferred_statements: Standard continuum/structural finite element methods can capture coupled NiTi contact behavior without novel constitutive laws.
paper_records.limitations: Numerical paper without new standalone experimental tests (benchmarked against Reedlunn).
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Confirms H0b feasibility for beam finite element modeling of NiTi wire bundles.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 4 (corotational beam contact formulation), Fig. 7 (validation against Reedlunn 2013)
paper_records.metadata_conflicts: Filename lists 2025 prefix, but paper publication year is verified as 2020 in Chinese JME.
